history.dynasty: Eastern Ganga (Anantavarman Chodaganga; Anangabhima Deva III); converted from Shaiva to Vaishnava in 11th-12th century
history.summary: Unique Vaishnava temple at Srikurmam village, Gara mandal (~15 km from Srikakulam town), dedicated to Lord Vishnu in his Kurma (tortoise) avatar - the only known pre-14th-century Indian temple of the Kurma avatar. Originally a Shiva temple (referred to as Kurmeswara); per the Prapannamrutam and the earliest temple inscription, Anantavarman Chodaganga of the Eastern Ganga dynasty converted it to a Vaishnava khetra in Saka 1035 CE, and Ramanuja's disciples (notably Naraharitirtha, disciple of Madhvacharya) established its Vaishnavite tradition. Built before the 11th century in a fusion of Kalinga and Dravidian architecture, with two dhvajasthambas (rare for a Vaishnava temple), 108 ekasila single-stone pillars with inscriptions (PILLAR-COUNT CONFLICT: templedairy says 201 pillars - flagged), and centuries-old Orissan Pattachitra murals. The west-facing deity combines a tortoise image and anthropomorphic Vishnu with Lakshmi; the sanctum allows direct devotee entry. Notable for the star-tortoise conservation park, daily abhisheka with devotee participation, and fame as a pitrukshetra for ancestor worship. Legend links it to King Swetha Chakravarthi's penance and the Swetha Pushkarani tank. Trustees: the Gajapathi Rajus of Vizianagaram; a commemorative postage stamp was issued on 11 April 2013. name: Sri Kurmanathaswamy Temple (Srikurmam)
town_description: Srikurmam is a village in Gara mandal of Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, ~15 km from Srikakulam town and 12.5 km from Arasavalli. It is a medieval Vaishnava centre famous for the Kurmanathaswamy temple, the only pre-14th-century temple dedicated to Vishnu's Kurma avatar.
